claims.claim: Paul Hermann Müller discovered DDT's insecticidal action in 1939 and was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1948; DDT was used in the second half of World War II against malaria and typhus.
claims.episode_span: The Swiss chemist Paul Hermann Müller, working at the J. R. Geigy laboratories in Basel, first demonstrated DDT's insecticidal power in 1939
claims.supporting_quote: DDT's insecticidal action was discovered by the Swiss chemist Paul Hermann Müller in 1939. DDT was used in the second half of World War II to limit the spread of the insect-borne diseases malaria and typhus among civilians and troops. Müller was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1948

claims.claim: During the Allied anti-typhus campaign in Naples in 1943-44, over a million people were dusted with DDT powder in the first mass-use campaign of the insecticide, and it was credited as the crucial factor in controlling the outbreak.
claims.episode_span: U.S. Army typhus control teams in Naples pumped handheld sprayers filled with a 10 percent DDT solution over the heads and clothing of more than a million refugees and soldiers
claims.source_title: Typhus in Naples, 1943-44: A Study in Vector Control - Wellcome Centre for Ethics and Humanities
claims.supporting_quote: The employment of the new insecticide DDT as an anti-typhus disinfectant has been highlighted as the crucial factor in controlling the outbreak: over a million inhabitants – men, women, and children – were 'dusted' with DDT powder in the first campaign to make mass use of it.

claims.claim: DDT's metabolite DDE interferes with calcium transport during eggshell formation, producing dose-dependent eggshell thinning in birds.
claims.episode_span: its metabolite DDE interferes with calcium deposition during eggshell formation in birds of prey
claims.supporting_quote: strong evidence indicates that p , p ' -DDE inhibits calcium ATPase in the membrane of the shell gland and reduces the transport of calcium carbonate from blood into the eggshell gland. This results in a dose-dependent thickness reduction.

claims.claim: The final DDD application to Clear Lake was in 1957, after which western grebes were found dead with high concentrations of DDD in their tissues.
claims.episode_span: after which western grebe populations crashed and tissue samples showed concentrations 80,000 times higher than in the surrounding water
claims.supporting_quote: The final application of DDD to Clear Lake was made in 1957 (Cook 1963). Numbers of western grebe were found dead, their tissues containing high concentrations of DDD.

claims.claim: Silent Spring was serialized in The New Yorker in June 1962, appearing in three parts in the June 16, June 23 and June 30 issues.
claims.episode_span: Rachel Carson's Silent Spring, serialized in The New Yorker in June 1962 and published as a book that September
claims.supporting_quote: Silent Spring initially appeared serialized in three parts in the June 16, June 23, and June 30, 1962, issues of The New Yorker magazine

claims.claim: President Kennedy's Science Advisory Committee reviewed the pesticide evidence and issued its report on May 15, 1963, largely backing Carson's scientific claims.
claims.episode_span: President Kennedy directed the Science Advisory Committee to review the evidence; its 1963 report confirmed the hazards to wildlife and called for tighter controls
claims.supporting_quote: Carson testified before President John F. Kennedy 's Science Advisory Committee, which issued its report on May 15, 1963, largely backing Carson's scientific claims

claims.claim: In the summer of 1972, after seven months of EPA hearings, Administrator Ruckelshaus announced the cancellation of most uses of DDT while exempting public-health uses under some conditions.
claims.episode_span: in 1972 banned DDT for most agricultural uses while allowing continued public-health applications
claims.supporting_quote: The EPA held seven months of hearings in 1971–1972, with scientists giving evidence for and against DDT. In the summer of 1972, Ruckelshaus announced the cancellation of most uses of DDT – exempting public health uses under some conditions.

claims.claim: In 2006 the WHO reversed its longstanding policy against DDT and recommended its use as an indoor residual pesticide in regions where malaria is a major problem.
claims.episode_span: the World Health Organization, facing persistent malaria mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, endorsed limited indoor DDT spraying again in 2006
claims.supporting_quote: In 2006 WHO reversed a longstanding policy against DDT by recommending that it be used as an indoor pesticide in regions where malaria is a major problem.
